summary.text: Magistral Small 1.2 is a 24B-parameter reasoning model from Mistral AI, built on Mistral Small 3.2 and released on 17 September 2025 on Mistral's API and as Apache 2.0 open weights. It accepts text and images; Mistral says a quantized version fits on a single RTX 4090 or a 32GB MacBook, and the weights stayed available after the API retirement in July 2026.

contextWindowTokens.note: The paper gives context lengths up to 256k tokens, and 128k for the reasoning checkpoints.

openWeights.note: Base, Instruct and Reasoning weights for all three sizes under Apache 2.0.

changes.text: Adds a 14B size alongside 3B and 8B.
Each size comes with a separate reasoning checkpoint next to the base and instruct checkpoints.
All checkpoints accept image input through a 410M-parameter vision encoder copied from Mistral Small 3.1 Base.
Trained by pruning and distilling from Mistral Small 3.1 on between 1 and 3 trillion tokens, according to the paper.

relations.note: The paper says all Ministral 3 models descend from Mistral Small 3.1 through Cascade Distillation: iterative pruning plus continued pretraining with logit distillation from the parent. The vision encoder is copied from Mistral Small 3.1 Base.

summary.text: Ministral 3 is a series of dense Mistral AI language models in 3B, 8B and 14B sizes aimed at edge and local use, released on 2 December 2025 with Mistral Large 3. Each size has base, instruct and reasoning checkpoints with image input under Apache 2.0; Mistral's paper says all were derived from Mistral Small 3.1 by pruning and distillation.

Has a context window of 256k tokens.

The models overview lists Large 3 as the alternative for the retired Large 1.0 and 2.0 endpoints, but Medium 3.5 for Large 2.1 (24.11).

summary.text: Mistral Large 3 is a sparse mixture-of-experts language model from Mistral AI with 675B total and 41B active parameters, released on 2 December 2025 with the Ministral 3 series as part of Mistral 3. It accepts text and images, has a 256k-token context window and is offered on Mistral's API, through cloud partners and as Apache 2.0 base and instruct weights.

access.note: Mistral API and AI Studio, Hugging Face, and NVIDIA (build.nvidia.com and NVIDIA NIM) at launch.

features.note: Configurable per request with the reasoning_effort parameter (none or high).

parameters.note: Mixture of experts with 128 experts, 4 active per token. The announcement gives 6B active parameters per token (8B including embedding and output layers); the docs and the model card give 6.5B active.

changes.text: Adds reasoning effort set per request (none or high) in the same model, instead of a separate Magistral reasoning model.
Moves to a mixture-of-experts design with 128 experts, 4 active per token, and 119B total parameters.
Has a context window of 256k tokens.
Mistral reports 40 percent less end-to-end completion time in a latency-optimized setup and three times more requests per second in a throughput-optimized setup than Small 3.

summary.text: Mistral Small 4 is a mixture-of-experts model from Mistral AI with 119B total parameters, released on 16 March 2026 as Apache 2.0 open weights and on Mistral's API. Mistral describes it as its first model to combine the reasoning, multimodal and agentic coding capabilities of Magistral, Pixtral and Devstral, with reasoning effort set per request.

summary.text: Mistral Medium 3.5 is a dense 128B-parameter Mistral AI model that handles instruction following, reasoning and coding in one set of weights, with text and image input and a 256k-token context window. It was released on 28 April 2026 as open weights under a Modified MIT licence and on the API, and in May 2026 became the default model in Le Chat and Mistral Vibe, in public preview.

description.text: Mistral AI is a Paris-based AI company that says it was founded in April 2023. It develops open-weight and commercial language models, as well as models for code, OCR, speech, embeddings and moderation, and offers enterprises and governments AI products including developer tools, applications and compute. Its first model, Mistral 7B, was released in September 2023 under the Apache 2.0 licence.
